name: Maacah
overview: Maacah was a female member of the tribe of Benjamin known primarily as the wife of Jeiel. Her identity is grounded in her marital relationship, with no additional personal notes recorded. She appears in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles, which emphasize her place within the Benjaminite lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Maacah is presented as a proper name and may mean 'dull' or 'stupid.' There is no indication that the name was given by God, and no alternate titles or meanings are recorded beyond this possible interpretation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Maacah as the wife of Jeiel, as noted in 1 Chronicles 8:29 and 9:35. Beyond this marital relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Maacah's significance in Scripture lies in her role within the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin. As the wife of Jeiel, she contributes to the historical and tribal lineage that the chronicler seeks to preserve. While not a prominent figure in narrative events, her mention underscores the importance of family connections in God's providential plan as recorded in the Old Testament.
